The problem is a pure-bending case on a rectangular beam. No transverse force, no shear force, no point loads, no distributed loads exist; the only action on the section is a single internal sagging bending moment.
The applied bending moment is M = 4,000,000 N·mm, sagging (concave-upward) direction, taken as positive.
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and depth h = 120 mm.
The coordinate y is measured from the centroid (neutral axis), positive upward.
All computations use the unit system N, mm, and MPa throughout.
Assume small deformations, linear-elastic material (Hooke's law), and Euler-Bernoulli (plane-sections-remain-plane) beam kinematics.
State the cross-section second moment of area formula I = b*h³/12 and evaluate it for the given b and h.
State the governing bending-stress relation σ(y) = -M*y/I, consistent with the convention that y is positive upward and a positive sagging moment produces compression on the top fiber.
Compute and report the bending stress at y = 0 (neutral axis).
Compute and report the bending stress at the top fiber, y = +h/2 = +60 mm, and identify whether it is tensile or compressive.
Compute and report the bending stress at the bottom fiber, y = -h/2 = -60 mm, and identify whether it is tensile or compressive.
Express every numerical result in MPa with appropriate sign, and clearly label the top-fiber and bottom-fiber values.
